npcs.name: Moon-Bishop Hadoba
npcs.greet: The moons are dancing well tonight, walker. This one can always tell. Sit, and let Hadoba see what kind of shadow you cast.

npcs.name: Jo'vassa the Pilgrim
npcs.greet: This one has walked from Rimmen with bad knees and a good heart. Only a little further now. Only a little.

relics.name: Consecrated Moon Sugar
relics.desc: Sugar from the temple fields, blessed under both moons. Stolen once, to be cooked into skooma. Not anymore.

relics.name: Censer of Twin Light
relics.desc: A silver censer with two openings, one for each moon. It went dark when the Fane fell to the Dro-m'Athra.

mp_dark_moon: The censer flares, and for a breath both moons seem to hang low over the ruin, one silver, one pale red.
Do you see? The Dro-m'Athra are Khajiit who walked off the Lattice and into the dark between the moons. Namiira's children. They are not evil, exactly. They are lost, and they are hungry.
We do not hate them. We send them home. Sometimes home is very far away.
mp_two_moons_dance: Masser rises, then Secunda. Azadhi and a temple moon-singer turn slow circles on the steps, one following Jone, one following Jode, never touching, never apart.
This is the Dance. Every Khajiit dances it, from the crib to the pyre. Some dance it well. Most dance it badly. A few forget the steps.
Dance with us, walker. Badly is fine. The moons are patient.
mp_voice: The Mane has heard of a walker who carries pilgrims, feeds the fields, and sends the lost children of the dark moon home.
The Mane has many voices. Priests, bishops, clan mothers. One more will not crowd the room. Kneel.
The Mane lays a braided cord of silver and red across your shoulders. In the temple, the moon-singers begin a low and very old song.

quests.title: The Riddle'Thar
quests.offer: I'd like to learn the ways of the Moon-Priests.
quests.pitch: Then you must first learn the Riddle'Thar, the order the moons gave our people when we were scattered and quarrelling. It is not difficult. It is only true. Walk with Azadhi under the moons tonight, and come back and tell Hadoba what you saw.
quests.desc: Moon-Bishop Hadoba of Torval agreed to teach me the faith of the Khajiit, beginning with the Riddle'Thar, the divine order of the moons.

objectives.topic: The Moon-Bishop sent me to walk with you.
objectives.reply: Good. Hadoba only sends those who might listen. We will wait for the moons together. They are always late, and always exactly on time.

objectives.topic: The moons are up. What am I looking for?
objectives.reply: Jone and Jode. Masser and Secunda. They move in a pattern, the Lattice, and a Khajiit's shape depends on how they stood at birth. All of us, cathay and senche and the little alfiq, are one people dancing under two lights. That is the first riddle.

choices.label: That every shape of Khajiit is one people.
choices.reply: Yes. The Riddle'Thar ended our clan wars by reminding us whose children we are. Welcome, Initiate.

choices.label: That the moons move in a pattern nobody can change.
choices.reply: Hm. Nobody should change. Some try. That is a story for later. Still: welcome, Initiate.

quests.outro: I watched the moons rise with Moon-Priest Azadhi and learned the first lesson of the Riddle'Thar. Moon-Bishop Hadoba accepted me as an Initiate.

consequence.summary: I watched the moons rise with Moon-Priest Azadhi and learned the first lesson of the Riddle'Thar. Moon-Bishop Hadoba accepted me as an Initiate.

quests.title: Sweetness of the Lattice
quests.offer: What would you have an Initiate do?
quests.pitch: Moon sugar is the Lattice made solid, the light of the moons caught in a grain. Skooma-cooks have raided the temple fields and carried our sugar to a camp south of the city, to boil it into poison. Bring it home before it is ruined.
quests.desc: Skooma-cooks raided the temple's moon sugar fields outside Torval. Hadoba sent me to recover the consecrated sugar before it was boiled into skooma.

objectives.text: Find the skooma-cooks' camp south of Torval

objectives.journal: Two of them were too far gone on their own product to feel the blows. I felt sorry for them, a little, afterwards.

objectives.text: Return the sugar to Moon-Bishop Hadoba
objectives.reply: The moons thank you, and so does Hadoba's sweet tooth. Remember: sugar is holy. Skooma is sugar that has forgotten what it is for. So are some Khajiit.

quests.outro: I broke up a skooma camp outside Torval and returned the temple's consecrated moon sugar to Hadoba.

consequence.summary: I broke up a skooma camp outside Torval and returned the temple's consecrated moon sugar to Hadoba.

quests.title: The Pilgrim's Path
quests.offer: You look like you could use company on the road.
quests.pitch: Company, and a sword to go with it. This one is walking to the Moon Temple in the hills to give thanks for a grandson. The road is full of bandits who think pilgrims carry gold. This one carries only sugar cakes, but bandits do not ask first.
quests.desc: Jo'vassa, an old Khajiit pilgrim, asked me to walk with him from Torval to the Moon Temple in the hills, where he means to give thanks for his grandson's birth.

objectives.text: Escort Jo'vassa to the Moon Temple
Drive off the bandits waylaying pilgrims
objectives.journal: The bandits had a senche-tiger on a chain. When its keeper fell, it simply lay down and purred. Jo'vassa fed it a sugar cake.

objectives.text: See Jo'vassa to the temple steps
objectives.topic: You made it. How are the knees?
objectives.reply: Terrible, and full of gratitude. This one will pray for his grandson, and then for you. Tell Hadoba that Jo'vassa says you walk well.

quests.outro: I escorted the pilgrim Jo'vassa safely to the Moon Temple, clearing the bandits who prey on the faithful along the way.

consequence.summary: I escorted the pilgrim Jo'vassa safely to the Moon Temple, clearing the bandits who prey on the faithful along the way.

quests.title: Children of the Dark Moon
quests.desc: Moongrave Fane, an old temple west of Torval, has fallen silent. Azadhi believes the Dro-m'Athra, Khajiit spirits lost to the darkness between the moons, have claimed it.

objectives.reply: Moongrave Fane has gone dark. Its keeper's censer burned for three hundred years and now it does not. Only the Dro-m'Athra put out a light like that. Go, and if the censer can be lit again, bring it to me.

objectives.text: Send the Dro-m'Athra back into the dark
Destroy the Dro-m'Athra who snuffed the censer
objectives.journal: Ash-Whisker had been the Fane's keeper once. I could see the old priest's cord still around its neck, gone black as the rest of it.

objectives.text: Bring the censer to Azadhi in Torval
objectives.topic: The Fane is cleansed. Its keeper was among them.
objectives.reply: Then he is home now, or closer to it. Look, the censer remembers.

quests.outro: I cleansed Moongrave Fane of the Dro-m'Athra, including the lost spirit of its own keeper, and brought the temple's censer back to Azadhi, who lit it again.

consequence.summary: I cleansed Moongrave Fane of the Dro-m'Athra, including the lost spirit of its own keeper, and brought the temple's censer back to Azadhi, who lit it again.

quests.title: The Two-Moons Dance
quests.desc: Hadoba has sent me to the Moon Temple, where Azadhi will teach me the Two-Moons Dance, the ritual that is also a way of life. Hadoba warns me that the darkness does not like to watch it.

objectives.text: Wait for both moons to rise

objectives.topic: I'm ready, though I don't know the steps.
objectives.reply: Nobody does. That is the point.

choices.label: Follow Jone, the bright moon of law and order.
choices.reply: Steady steps. Good. Jone keeps the pattern so the rest of us can stray a little.

choices.label: Follow Jode, the pale moon of change.
choices.reply: Quick steps. Good. Jode reminds the pattern that it is alive.

objectives.text: Drive off the shadow that comes to break the Dance
objectives.journal: The shadow came out of the gap between the moons' light. It did not like being seen. When it fled, the singers did not even miss a note.

objectives.topic: It's gone. Did I ruin the Dance?
objectives.reply: Ruin it? Walker, that was the Dance. The darkness always comes to watch. The trick is to keep dancing. Hadoba will hear of this, and then, this one suspects, so will the Mane.

quests.outro: I joined the Two-Moons Dance at the Moon Temple and drove off a shadow of Namiira that came to break it. Azadhi says the Mane will hear of it.

consequence.summary: I joined the Two-Moons Dance at the Moon Temple and drove off a shadow of Namiira that came to break it. Azadhi says the Mane will hear of it.

quests.title: Voice of the Mane
quests.desc: The Mane has summoned me to Riverhold. Hadoba warns that Renrijra Krin rebels have been seen near the city, and they would like nothing better than to embarrass the Mane in front of the faithful.

objectives.reply: The Mane knows. The Mane also knows that knives are waiting on the hill road behind the palace. The Renrijra Krin believe a dead priest makes a fine joke. Show them it does not.

objectives.text: Ambush the Renrijra Krin on the hill road
objectives.journal: The Laughing Knife laughed right up until the end. I think it was genuine. The Renrijra find a great many things funny that are not.

objectives.topic: The hill road is clear. No one is laughing.
objectives.reply: Good. Then come before the moons and the people.

quests.outro: I stopped a Renrijra Krin ambush outside Riverhold. Before the moons and the faithful, the Mane named me a Moon-Bishop and one of the Voices of the Mane.

consequence.summary: I stopped a Renrijra Krin ambush outside Riverhold. Before the moons and the faithful, the Mane named me a Moon-Bishop and one of the Voices of the Mane.
